title: Story Stones
strapline: A pocketful of pebbles that turn into any story you can imagine.
intent: Children invent and tell their own stories, choosing characters and events as they draw stones from the bag.
Children build narrative language and structure — and then, gone; suddenly; happily ever after.
Children use symbols to stand for ideas — a painted moon means night, a wave means the sea — early reading of pictures.
Children develop confidence in speaking and telling, holding a listener's attention.
Children connect spoken storytelling to books, making up tales they'll later want to write down.
implementation: Make or gather smooth stones painted with simple pictures — characters, animals, weather, places, objects.
Model telling first: draw a stone, start a story, draw the next, let the story grow from what appears.
Then hand over — let children pull the stones and tell, following their story wherever it goes.
Feed in story connectives as you play: 'and then...', 'but suddenly...', 'in the end...'.
Keep the stones in a beautiful bag or basket so drawing one feels a little bit magic.
Offer a story-map cloth or a circle to lay the stones out and remember the order of the tale.
Sometimes scribe a child's story or record it, so they see their words matter and can hear them again.
key_questions: What happens next — which stone will you draw?
How does your story begin? How will it end?
What does this picture make you think of?
Can you tell me your story again from the start?

impact.text: Children make up and tell their own stories with a clear thread.
Children use story language and connectives as they tell.
Children read the picture symbols and give them meaning.
Children sequence events into a beginning, middle and end.
Children speak confidently and hold a listener's attention.
Children stay engaged, extending and elaborating their tale.

enhancements: Themed stone sets — a fairy-tale set, a woodland set, an under-the-sea set.
A story-map cloth or a circle of felt to lay the stones along.
A recording device so children can hear their stories back.
Blank stones and pens for children to make their own characters.
A story dice alongside for an extra element of surprise.
A cosy story tent to tell tales in with a friend.

playing_exploring: Children choose stones and let the story unfold from chance.
They play freely with characters, settings and events.
active_learning: Children develop a story over time, wanting to reach an ending.
They return to storytelling for the pleasure of being the author.
creating_thinking: Children link the images into a coherent, imaginative tale.
They plan where their story is going and adapt when a new stone appears.
